Based on visual inspection and supported by floor plans, the warehouse space was used for various types of electronic instrumentation fitted into diagnostic trailers that were used across the NNSS, particularly during nuclear tests. With a 240-ft-long loading dock with electrical power outlets and fronting Mercury Highway, diagnostic trailers could be pulled up to the loading dock to either be fitted with electronic equipment or deliver their equipment back to the Technical Support Building for review and use another time. Because the building was constructed after the 1963 Limited Test Ban Treaty, the warehouse and the equipment that it housed would have been related to underground tests that took place at various locations in the forward areas of the NNSS. The building is still being used as a storage and warehouse facility. Its associated office space is now mostly empty and unused. NRHP ELIGIBILITY The Technical Support Building, 06-CP-65 (SHPO Resource # B18910), is not recommended eligible for listing in the NRHP as an individual resource. It was previously determined eligible as a contributing element to the Area 6 Control Point Historic District (O’Neill et al. 2021; Reed 2022) and it remains eligible as such. Criterion A. To be eligible for the National Register under Criterion A, properties must be associated with events that have made a significant contribution to the broad patterns of our history. The Technical Support Building is associated with nuclear testing on the NNSS. It is part of the Area 6 Control Point which was responsible for the timing and firing of nuclear tests on the NNSS. While it is known that the building was used both as engineering office and laboratory space and as a warehouse and power supply for the diagnostics trailer fleet, it is unclear exactly what role it played for any given test or in any specific scientific role on the NNSS. It cannot, therefore, be tied to a specific test or series of tests nor to any important and specific scientific developments. As such, Building 06-CP-65 does not appear to be eligible under Criterion A. Criterion B. Properties may be eligible for the National Register if they are associated with the lives of persons significant in our past. While many people worked at the Technical Support Building either as part of the warehouse staff or associated with the administration functions that took place within it, the building does not appear to be associated with any significant individuals. Therefore, Building 06-CP-65 is not recommended eligible for listing under Criterion B. Criterion C. Properties may be eligible under Criterion C if they embody the distinctive characteristics of a type, period, or method of construction, or that represent the work of a master, or that possess high artistic values.
